front: Effect of pH on Fe(II) stability
back: Air oxidises Fe(II) far more easily in alkali (E⦵cell +0.96 V) than in acid (+0.46 V).
E⦵ falls from +0.77 V (aqua) to +0.36 V (cyanide): iron(III) is stabilised; [Fe(CN)₆]³⁻ is a weaker oxidant.
Fe²⁺ in haem (4 N of porphyrin + protein) binds O₂ reversibly; CO binds far more strongly (poisoning).
Haem proteins in the electron-transport chain; iron cycles Fe²⁺ ⇌ Fe³⁺ + e⁻ to pass electrons.
Iron joined to a more reactive metal (Zn, Mg; more negative E⦵), which is oxidised instead of the iron.
